notFoundDesc: This list exists only for fibrous dysplasia (FD/MAS) for now, because the quotations come from a guideline written about that disease.
title: Baseline evaluation in FD/MAS — what the guideline lists
lede: Each row carries the sentence from the guideline it rests on. The “result / date” box is empty — it is space to write in.
colWhy: Why it is on the list
sourceLine: Every quotation is from: Javaid MK et al., Best practice management guidelines for fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright syndrome, Orphanet J Rare Dis 2019;14:139 (PMID 31196103). The sentences come from the sections “Diagnosis”, “Histological and genetic characterisation”, “Staging of FD/MAS” and “Management of Craniofacial FD”.
authorshipLine: The GeneQuest Foundation put this list together from that guideline; the guideline authors have not reviewed or approved it.
safetyLine: This is not medical advice and not a referral. Which of these applies to your child is for your doctor to say.
metaDescription: A printable list: the tests the FD/MAS guideline (Javaid 2019) names in the baseline evaluation — each with the verbatim sentence behind it and space for a result and a date.

labs.name: Blood tests — bone panel
labs.why: The panel the guideline lists in the baseline evaluation: renal profile, alkaline phosphatase, bicarbonate, albumin-adjusted calcium, phosphate, 25OH vitamin D, parathyroid hormone.
labs.quote: Bone-related laboratory testing … should include a standard biochemistry screen of renal profile, total alkaline phosphatase, bicarbonate, albumin-adjusted serum calcium, phosphate …, 25OH-vitamin D and parathyroid hormone.
labs.whenQuote: Staging should be considered at the time of presentation with suspected FD/MAS taking into account age and clinical presentation.

phosphate.name: Fasting phosphate
phosphate.why: The guideline describes renal phosphate wasting as important to diagnose, because it carries fracture risk.
phosphate.quote: Abnormal phosphate homeostasis, specifically renal phosphate wasting leading to hypophosphatemia, is important to diagnose as it is an important predictor of future fracture risk, as well as other complications.
phosphate.when: When polyostotic disease is suspected; blood drawn fasting.
phosphate.whenQuote: In all subjects with suspected polyostotic disease, baseline overnight fasting phosphate levels should be checked.

wholeBody.name: Whole-body imaging
wholeBody.why: Shows how much of the skeleton is involved — bone scintigraphy, whole-body MR, or low-dose 2D/3D radiography.
wholeBody.quote: To evaluate the extent of FD, whole body imaging using bone scintigraphy, whole body MR or low-dose 2D/3D radiography (e.g. EOS), to determine the presence and extent of skeletal involvement should be considered for all patients ≥ age 5 years.
wholeBody.when: From age 5; in a child without symptoms the guideline describes waiting until then.
wholeBody.whenQuote: Due to the possibility of false negative results, whole body imaging should be delayed in asymptomatic children until age 5 … and when the child can tolerate an MRI without general anaesthesia.

radiographs.name: X-ray of the involved bone in two planes
radiographs.why: Lesions of clinical significance found on whole-body imaging are, in the guideline, imaged with conventional radiographs of the whole bone.
radiographs.quote: Areas of clinically significant axial and appendicular FD identified on bone scintigraphy should be imaged with conventional radiographs in two planes of the whole bone.

craniofacialCt.name: Craniofacial CT, fine cut (≤ 1 mm)
craniofacialCt.why: Radiological assessment of the craniofacial skeleton in the guideline covers facial and orthognathic series plus a fine-cut CT.
craniofacialCt.quote: Radiological assessment includes standard radiological facial and orthognathic series and fine cut CT 1 mm or less slice thickness.
craniofacialCt.when: When lesions involve the skull or the facial skeleton; in children the scan is repeated.
craniofacialCt.whenQuote: Baseline and periodic CT scans of the head should be performed in children, usually every 2 years or less frequently based on the localisation and severity of the lesion(s).

hearing.name: Hearing assessment
hearing.why: Where the skull base is involved, the guideline lists a hearing assessment every year.
hearing.quote: An assessment of hearing should be performed annually in all patients with skull base disease.
hearing.when: Annually, where the skull base is involved.

thyroid.name: Thyroid — TSH, free T4, T3, ultrasound
thyroid.why: The thyroid is one of the extra-skeletal features of FD/MAS; the guideline lists these for all patients.
thyroid.quote: All patients should have a targeted history and physical examination, measurement of TSH, free T4 & total or free T3 and thyroid ultrasound to characterise subclinical involvement consistent with MAS.

pituitary.name: Pituitary — IGF-1, growth hormone, prolactin
pituitary.why: Growth hormone excess is one of the extra-skeletal features of FD/MAS; the guideline lists these three for all patients.
pituitary.quote: All patients should have a random blood test for IGF-1, growth hormone (GH) and prolactin measurements.
pituitary.when: All patients; pituitary MRI where the blood results are abnormal.
pituitary.whenQuote: Pituitary MRI is indicated in case of abnormal biochemistry …, although a normal pituitary MRI does not rule out the possibility of GH excess as the affected tissue may not be detectable by MRI.

testicular.name: Testicular ultrasound (boys)
testicular.why: The guideline lists it for all boys and men, including those without symptoms.
testicular.quote: All males should have a testicular ultrasound at baseline … and after age 5 to characterise subclinical involvement consistent with MAS.

ovarian.name: FSH, LH, estradiol and pelvic ultrasound (girls)
ovarian.why: The guideline lists these for girls who have symptoms.
ovarian.quote: If symptomatic, girls should have a random blood FSH, LH, estradiol and pelvic ultrasound.

growth.name: Growth curve and bone age
growth.why: The guideline lists a review of the growth curve and a standardised bone age examination for all children.
growth.quote: All children should have a review of their growth curve for linear growth acceleration or deceleration and a standardised bone age examination.

adrenal.name: Cortisol — adrenal axis
adrenal.why: The guideline lists these where there is clinical suspicion of hypercortisolism.
adrenal.quote: In case of clinical suspicion of current hypercortisolism, 24-h urinary free cortisol, low dose dexamethasone suppression test, diurnal cortisol and adrenal CT should be performed.
adrenal.when: On suspicion; an ACTH stimulation test where neonatal hypercortisolism is in the history.
adrenal.whenQuote: The ACTH stimulation test should be performed in all patients with a known or suspected history of neonatal hypercortisolism.

skin.name: Skin examination — café-au-lait macules
skin.why: The guideline lists a skin examination for all patients, looking for typical café-au-lait macules.
skin.quote: A physical examination should be performed in all patients for typical café-au-lait macules …

gnas.name: GNAS genetic test
gnas.why: The guideline lists it where the diagnosis is in question — especially for a single lesion in the skull. A positive result is informative; a negative one from blood does not rule FD out.
gnas.quote: A genetic diagnosis is recommended where the diagnosis is in question. This especially applies to isolated/monostotic lesions in the skull…
gnas.whenQuote: Use of blood for mutation analysis cannot exclude the diagnosis of monostotic FD, but a positive result is informative.
